# dsyevr

> Computes the eigenvalues and, optionally, the left and/or right eigenvectors for symmetric matrices.

<section class="usage">

## Usage

```js
import dsyevr from '@rreusser/blahpack/lapack/dsyevr';
```

### Layout API

Takes a storage layout (`order`) and leading dimensions, like CBLAS/LAPACKE.

```js
dsyevr(
    order,
    jobz, range, uplo,
    N,
    A, LDA,
    vl, vu, il, iu, abstol,
    m,
    w, strideW,
    Z, LDZ,
    ISUPPZ, strideISUPPZ,
    WORK,
    IWORK
) → integer
```

| Parameter | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `order` | `Layout` | Storage layout ('row-major' or 'column-major') |
| `jobz` | `"no-vectors" \| "compute-vectors"` | `'no-vectors'`: Compute eigenvalues only; `'compute-vectors'`: Compute eigenvalues and eigenvectors. |
| `range` | `"all" \| "value" \| "index"` | `'all'`: all eigenvalues will be found. `'value'`: all eigenvalues in the half-open interval (VL,VU] will be found. `'index'`: the IL-th through IU-th eigenvalues will be found. For `range === 'value'` or `range === 'index'` and IU - IL < N - 1, DSTEBZ and DSTEIN are called. |
| `uplo` | `MatrixTriangle` | `'upper'`: Upper triangle of A is stored; `'lower'`: Lower triangle of A is stored. |
| `N` | `NonNegativeInteger` | The order of the matrix A.<br>Requires `N ≥ 0` |
| `A` | `Float64Array`<br><sub>N × N</sub> | **in/out** · On entry, the symmetric matrix A. On exit, the lower triangle (if `uplo === 'lower'`) or the upper triangle (if `uplo === 'upper'`) of A, including the diagonal, is destroyed. |
| ↳ `LDA` | `PositiveInteger` | Leading dimension of `A`<br>Requires `LDA ≥ max(1, N)` |
| `vl` | `number` | If `range === 'value'`, the lower bound of the interval to be searched for eigenvalues. |
| `vu` | `number` | If `range === 'value'`, the upper bound of the interval to be searched for eigenvalues.<br>Rejects `range === 'value' && (N > 0 && vu <= vl)` |
| `il` | `integer` | If `range === 'index'`, the index of the smallest eigenvalue to be returned. 1 <= IL <= IU <= N, if N > 0.<br>Rejects `range !== 'value' && range === 'index' && (il < 1 \|\| il > max(1, N))` |
| `iu` | `integer` | If `range === 'index'`, the index of the largest eigenvalue to be returned. 1 <= IL <= IU <= N, if N > 0.<br>Rejects `range !== 'value' && range === 'index' && (iu < min(N, il) \|\| iu > N)` |
| `abstol` | `number` | The absolute error tolerance for the eigenvalues. |
| `m` | `Int32Array` | **out** · Output (length-1 array): the total number of eigenvalues found |
| `w` | `Float64Array`<br><sub>length N</sub> | **out** · The first M elements contain the selected eigenvalues in ascending order. |
| ↳ `strideW` | `integer` | Stride length for `w` |
| `Z` | `Float64Array`<br><sub>N × (range === 'index' ? iu - il + 1 : N)</sub> | **out** · If `jobz === 'compute-vectors'`, then if INFO = 0, the first M columns of Z contain the orthonormal eigenvectors of the matrix A corresponding to the selected eigenvalues, with the i-th column of Z holding the eigenvector associated with W(i). |
| ↳ `LDZ` | `PositiveInteger` | Leading dimension of `Z`<br>Rejects `ldz < 1 \|\| (jobz === 'compute-vectors' && ldz < N)` |
| `ISUPPZ` | `Int32Array`<br><sub>length 2 * max(1, m)</sub> | **out** · The support of the eigenvectors in Z, i.e., the indices indicating the nonzero elements in Z (0-based). |
| ↳ `strideISUPPZ` | `integer` | Stride length for `ISUPPZ` |
| `WORK` | `Float64Array \| null`<br><sub>length ≥ max(1, 26 * N)</sub> | **out** · Caller-provided workspace of at least `max( 1, 26 * N )` elements; if `null`, a workspace of the reference's optimal size (LWKOPT, with the DSYTRD block size from `ilaenv`) is allocated |
| `IWORK` | `Int32Array \| null`<br><sub>length ≥ max(1, 10 * N)</sub> | **out** · Caller-provided workspace of at least `max( 1, 10 * N )` elements |

<details>
<summary>Reference notes for each argument (the reference implementation's own documentation; 1-based indices)</summary>

- `jobz`:

  -   `= 'N'`: Compute eigenvalues only;
  -   `= 'V'`: Compute eigenvalues and eigenvectors.
- `range`:

  -   `= 'A'`: all eigenvalues will be found.
  -   `= 'V'`: all eigenvalues in the half-open interval (`VL`,`VU`\] will be found.
  -   `= 'I'`: the `IL`-th through `IU`-th eigenvalues will be found. For `RANGE = 'V'` or 'I' and $\mathrm{IU} - \mathrm{IL} < N - 1$, DSTEBZ and DSTEIN are called
- `uplo`:

  -   `= 'U'`: Upper triangle of A is stored;
  -   `= 'L'`: Lower triangle of A is stored.
- `N`: The order of the matrix A. $N \ge 0$.
- `A`: On entry, the symmetric matrix A. If `UPLO = 'U'`, the leading N-by-N upper triangular part of A contains the upper triangular part of the matrix A. If `UPLO = 'L'`, the leading N-by-N lower triangular part of A contains the lower triangular part of the matrix A. On exit, the lower triangle (if `UPLO='L'`) or the upper triangle (if `UPLO='U'`) of A, including the diagonal, is destroyed.
- `vl`: If `RANGE='V'`, the lower bound of the interval to be searched for eigenvalues. $\mathrm{VL} < \mathrm{VU}$. Not referenced if `RANGE = 'A'` or 'I'.
- `vu`: If `RANGE='V'`, the upper bound of the interval to be searched for eigenvalues. $\mathrm{VL} < \mathrm{VU}$. Not referenced if `RANGE = 'A'` or 'I'.
- `il`: If `RANGE='I'`, the index of the smallest eigenvalue to be returned. $1 \le \mathrm{IL} \le \mathrm{IU} \le N$, if $N > 0$; `IL = 1` and `IU = 0` if $N = 0$. Not referenced if `RANGE = 'A'` or 'V'.
- `iu`: If `RANGE='I'`, the index of the largest eigenvalue to be returned. $1 \le \mathrm{IL} \le \mathrm{IU} \le N$, if $N > 0$; `IL = 1` and `IU = 0` if $N = 0$. Not referenced if `RANGE = 'A'` or 'V'.
- `abstol`: The absolute error tolerance for the eigenvalues. An approximate eigenvalue is accepted as converged when it is determined to lie in an interval \[a,b\] of width less than or equal to

  $$
  \mathrm{ABSTOL} + \mathrm{EPS} \, \max ( |a|,|b| )
  $$

  where EPS is the machine precision. If `ABSTOL` is less than or equal to zero, then EPS\*\|T\| will be used in its place, where \|T\| is the 1-norm of the tridiagonal matrix obtained by reducing A to tridiagonal form.

  See "Computing Small Singular Values of Bidiagonal Matrices with Guaranteed High Relative Accuracy," by Demmel and Kahan, LAPACK Working Note #3.

  If high relative accuracy is important, set `ABSTOL` to DLAMCH( 'Safe minimum' ). Doing so will guarantee that eigenvalues are computed to high relative accuracy when possible in future releases. The current code does not make any guarantees about high relative accuracy, but future releases will. See J. Barlow and J. Demmel, "Computing Accurate Eigensystems of Scaled Diagonally Dominant Matrices", LAPACK Working Note #7, for a discussion of which matrices define their eigenvalues to high relative accuracy.
- `m`: The total number of eigenvalues found. $0 \le M \le N$. If `RANGE = 'A'`, $M = N$, and if `RANGE = 'I'`, $M = \mathrm{IU}-\mathrm{IL}+1$.
- `w`: The first M elements contain the selected eigenvalues in ascending order.
- `Z`: If `JOBZ = 'V'`, then if `INFO = 0`, the first M columns of Z contain the orthonormal eigenvectors of the matrix A corresponding to the selected eigenvalues, with the i-th column of Z holding the eigenvector associated with `W(i)`. If `JOBZ = 'N'`, then Z is not referenced. Note: the user must ensure that at least max(1,M) columns are supplied in the array Z; if `RANGE = 'V'`, the exact value of M is not known in advance and an upper bound must be used. Supplying N columns is always safe.
- `ISUPPZ`: The support of the eigenvectors in Z, i.e., the indices indicating the nonzero elements in Z. The i-th eigenvector is nonzero only in elements ISUPPZ( 2\*i-1 ) through ISUPPZ( 2\*i ). This is an output of DSTEMR (tridiagonal matrix). The support of the eigenvectors of A is typically 1:N because of the orthogonal transformations applied by DORMTR. Implemented only for `RANGE = 'A'` or 'I' and $\mathrm{IU} - \mathrm{IL} = N - 1$
- `WORK`: On exit, if `INFO = 0`, `WORK(1)` returns the optimal `LWORK`.
- `IWORK`: On exit, if `INFO = 0`, `IWORK(1)` returns the optimal `LWORK`.

</details>

**Returns** `integer`: status code (0 = success)

**Throws**

- `TypeError` first argument must be a valid order
- `TypeError` second argument must be one of the following: "no-vectors", "compute-vectors"
- `TypeError` third argument must be one of the following: "all", "index", "value"
- `TypeError` fourth argument must be a valid matrix triangle
- `RangeError` fifth argument must be a nonnegative integer
- `RangeError` seventh argument must be greater than or equal to `max( 1, N )`
- `RangeError` ninth argument is invalid (rejected when `range === "value" && ( N > 0 && vu <= vl )`)
- `RangeError` tenth argument is invalid (rejected when `range !== "value" && range === "index" && ( il < 1 \|\| il > max( 1, N ) )`)
- `RangeError` eleventh argument is invalid (rejected when `range !== "value" && range === "index" && ( iu < min( N, il ) \|\| iu > N )`)
- `RangeError` seventeenth argument is invalid (column-major: rejected when `LDZ < 1 \|\| ( jobz === "compute-vectors" && LDZ < N )`)
- `RangeError` seventeenth argument is invalid (row-major: rejected when `LDZ < 1 \|\| ( jobz === "compute-vectors" && LDZ < max( 1, range === "index" ? iu - il + 1 : N ) )`)
- `TypeError` if a string argument is not a valid option

### Strided (strided) API

Takes explicit strides and offsets for every array. Use it for views, sub-matrices and non-unit strides.

```js
dsyevr.strided(
    jobz, range, uplo,
    N,
    A, strideA1, strideA2, offsetA,
    vl, vu, il, iu, abstol,
    m,
    w, strideW, offsetW,
    Z, strideZ1, strideZ2, offsetZ,
    ISUPPZ, strideISUPPZ, offsetISUPPZ,
    WORK, strideWork, offsetWork,
    IWORK, strideIWork, offsetIWork
) → integer
```

Computes selected eigenvalues and, optionally, eigenvectors of a real.
symmetric matrix A.

Eigenvalues and eigenvectors can be selected by specifying either a range
of values or a range of indices for the desired eigenvalues.

Algorithm:
1. Scale the matrix if the norm is outside safe range
2. Reduce to tridiagonal form via dsytrd
3. For eigenvalues-only (all eigenvalues): use dsterf
4. Otherwise: use dstebz for eigenvalue bisection + dstein for eigenvectors
5. Transform eigenvectors back via dormtr
6. Sort eigenvalues and eigenvectors, undo scaling

Note: This implementation does not use DSTEMR (the MRRR algorithm).
It always uses the DSTEBZ+DSTEIN fallback path. For eigenvalues-only
with all eigenvalues requested, DSTERF is used instead.

M is an output parameter indicating the number of eigenvalues found.
It is returned via the out object: out.M.

Matrix shapes are logical (rows × columns). The reference's leading dimension (`LDA`, …) is replaced by the two strides and the offset.

| Parameter | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `jobz` | `"no-vectors" \| "compute-vectors"` | 'no-vectors' or 'compute-vectors' |
| `range` | `"all" \| "value" \| "index"` | 'all', 'value', or 'index' |
| `uplo` | `MatrixTriangle` | 'upper' or 'lower' |
| `N` | `NonNegativeInteger` | Order of the matrix A<br>Requires `N ≥ 0` |
| `A` | `Float64Array`<br><sub>N × N</sub> | **in/out** · Input/output symmetric matrix (destroyed on exit) |
| ↳ `strideA1` | `integer` | Stride of the first dimension of A |
| ↳ `strideA2` | `integer` | Stride of the second dimension of A |
| ↳ `offsetA` | `NonNegativeInteger` | Starting index for A |
| `vl` | `number` | Lower bound of eigenvalue interval (RANGE='value') |
| `vu` | `number` | Upper bound of eigenvalue interval (RANGE='value')<br>Rejects `range === 'value' && (N > 0 && vu <= vl)` |
| `il` | `integer` | Index of smallest eigenvalue to compute (1-based, RANGE='index')<br>Rejects `range !== 'value' && range === 'index' && (il < 1 \|\| il > max(1, N))` |
| `iu` | `integer` | Index of largest eigenvalue to compute (1-based, RANGE='index')<br>Rejects `range !== 'value' && range === 'index' && (iu < min(N, il) \|\| iu > N)` |
| `abstol` | `number` | Absolute tolerance for eigenvalues |
| `m` | `Int32Array` | **out** · Output (length-1 array): the total number of eigenvalues found |
| `w` | `Float64Array`<br><sub>length N</sub> | **out** · Output array for eigenvalues (length N) |
| ↳ `strideW` | `integer` | Stride for w |
| ↳ `offsetW` | `NonNegativeInteger` | Starting index for w |
| `Z` | `Float64Array`<br><sub>N × (range === 'index' ? iu - il + 1 : N)</sub> | **out** · Output eigenvector matrix (N x M) |
| ↳ `strideZ1` | `integer` | Stride of first dimension of Z |
| ↳ `strideZ2` | `integer` | Stride of second dimension of Z |
| ↳ `offsetZ` | `NonNegativeInteger` | Starting index for Z |
| `ISUPPZ` | `Int32Array`<br><sub>length 2 * max(1, m)</sub> | **out** · Support of eigenvectors (length 2\*M) |
| ↳ `strideISUPPZ` | `integer` | Stride for ISUPPZ |
| ↳ `offsetISUPPZ` | `NonNegativeInteger` | Starting index for ISUPPZ |
| `WORK` | `Float64Array`<br><sub>length ≥ max(1, 26 * N)</sub> | **out** · Workspace (length >= `max( 1, 26*N )`) |
| ↳ `strideWork` | `integer` | Stride for WORK |
| ↳ `offsetWork` | `NonNegativeInteger` | Starting index for WORK |
| `IWORK` | `Int32Array`<br><sub>length ≥ max(1, 10 * N)</sub> | **out** · Integer workspace (length >= `max( 1, 10*N )`) |
| ↳ `strideIWork` | `integer` | Stride for IWORK |
| ↳ `offsetIWork` | `NonNegativeInteger` | Starting index for IWORK |

**Returns** `integer`: status code (0 = success)

**Throws**

- `TypeError` first argument must be one of the following: "no-vectors", "compute-vectors"
- `TypeError` second argument must be one of the following: "all", "index", "value"
- `TypeError` third argument must be a valid matrix triangle
- `RangeError` fourth argument must be a nonnegative integer
- `RangeError` tenth argument is invalid (rejected when `range === "value" && ( N > 0 && vu <= vl )`)
- `RangeError` eleventh argument is invalid (rejected when `range !== "value" && range === "index" && ( il < 1 \|\| il > max( 1, N ) )`)
- `RangeError` twelfth argument is invalid (rejected when `range !== "value" && range === "index" && ( iu < min( N, il ) \|\| iu > N )`)

### Status codes

An `info` status code: `0` on success. A positive value reports a numerical condition such as a singular pivot or a failure to converge (see the description). Invalid arguments throw instead of returning a negative `info`. Returns immediately when `N === 0`.

The reference documents `INFO` as:

-   `= 0`: successful exit
-   `< 0`: if `INFO = -i`, the i-th argument had an illegal value
-   `> 0`: Internal error

<section class="examples">

## Examples

```js
import Float64Array from '@stdlib/array/float64/lib/index.js';
import Int32Array from '@stdlib/array/int32/lib/index.js';
import dsyevr from '@rreusser/blahpack/lapack/dsyevr';

// Symmetric 3x3 matrix (column-major; only the upper triangle is referenced):
const N = 3;
const data = [ 4.0, 1.0, 2.0, 1.0, 3.0, 0.5, 2.0, 0.5, 5.0 ];
let A = new Float64Array( data );
const w = new Float64Array( N );
const m = new Int32Array( 1 );
const Z = new Float64Array( N * N );
const ISUPPZ = new Int32Array( 2 * N );
const WORK = new Float64Array( 26 * N );
const IWORK = new Int32Array( 10 * N );

// Using the standard interface:
let info = dsyevr( 'column-major', 'compute-vectors', 'all', 'upper', N, A, N, 0.0, 0.0, 1, N, 0.0, m, w, 1, Z, N, ISUPPZ, 1, WORK, IWORK );
console.log( info, m[ 0 ], w, Z );

// Using the strided interface:
A = new Float64Array( data );
info = dsyevr.strided( 'compute-vectors', 'all', 'upper', N, A, 1, N, 0, 0.0, 0.0, 1, N, 0.0, m, w, 1, 0, Z, 1, N, 0, ISUPPZ, 1, 0, WORK, 1, 0, IWORK, 1, 0 );
console.log( info, m[ 0 ], w, Z );
```

</section>

<!-- /.examples -->

<section class="reference-notes">

## Reference notes

The mathematical description from the reference LAPACK 3.12.0 source of `DSYEVR`. Indices are the 1-based Fortran indices of the source.

### Purpose

DSYEVR computes selected eigenvalues and, optionally, eigenvectors of a real symmetric matrix A. Eigenvalues and eigenvectors can be selected by specifying either a range of values or a range of indices for the desired eigenvalues.

DSYEVR first reduces the matrix A to tridiagonal form T with a call to DSYTRD. Then, whenever possible, DSYEVR calls DSTEMR to compute the eigenspectrum using Relatively Robust Representations. DSTEMR computes eigenvalues by the dqds algorithm, while orthogonal eigenvectors are computed from various "good" L D L^T representations (also known as Relatively Robust Representations). Gram-Schmidt orthogonalization is avoided as far as possible. More specifically, the various steps of the algorithm are as follows.

For each unreduced block (submatrix) of T,

-   (a) Compute T - $\sigma$ $I = L$ D L^T, so that L and D define all the wanted eigenvalues to high relative accuracy. This means that small relative changes in the entries of D and L cause only small relative changes in the eigenvalues and eigenvectors. The standard (unfactored) representation of the tridiagonal matrix T does not have this property in general.
-   (b) Compute the eigenvalues to suitable accuracy. If the eigenvectors are desired, the algorithm attains full accuracy of the computed eigenvalues only right before the corresponding vectors have to be computed, see steps c) and d).
-   (c) For each cluster of close eigenvalues, select a new shift close to the cluster, find a new factorization, and refine the shifted eigenvalues to suitable accuracy.
-   (d) For each eigenvalue with a large enough relative separation compute the corresponding eigenvector by forming a rank revealing twisted factorization. Go back to (c) for any clusters that remain.

The desired accuracy of the output can be specified by the input parameter `ABSTOL`.

For more details, see DSTEMR's documentation and: - Inderjit S. Dhillon and Beresford N. Parlett: "Multiple representations

-   to compute orthogonal eigenvectors of symmetric tridiagonal matrices,"
-   Linear Algebra and its Applications, 387(1), pp. 1-28, August 2004.

- Inderjit Dhillon and Beresford Parlett: "Orthogonal Eigenvectors and

-   Relative Gaps," SIAM Journal on Matrix Analysis and Applications, Vol. 25,
-   2004. Also LAPACK Working Note 154.

- Inderjit Dhillon: "A new O(n^2) algorithm for the symmetric

-   tridiagonal eigenvalue/eigenvector problem",
-   Computer Science Division Technical Report No. UCB/CSD-97-971,
-   UC Berkeley, May 1997.

Note 1 : DSYEVR calls DSTEMR when the full spectrum is requested on machines which conform to the ieee-754 floating point standard. DSYEVR calls DSTEBZ and DSTEIN on non-ieee machines and when partial spectrum requests are made.

Normal execution of DSTEMR may create NaNs and infinities and hence may abort due to a floating point exception in environments which do not handle NaNs and infinities in the ieee standard default manner.

</section>
